newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end easier, Olivetti rebounds.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end easier, Olivetti rebounds.

text.p: Italian shares drifted down in a lacklustre day on Wednesday to close easier but were off the day's lows helped as the Dow Jones clawed back initial declines, with Olivetti one share to stand out after recent falls.

Dealers said Olivetti shares were due a technical bounce after hitting a record low of 555 lire a share on Tuesday, but uncertainty still remained over the group's accounts and investors hope some light may be shed on these areas at next week's meetings with analysts in Milan and London.
The all-share Mibtel ended off 0.86 percent at 9,403, while the Mib30 index was 1.0 percent off at 13,979.

Olivetti shares ended up 2.71 percent at 583.2 lire, but Carlo De Benedetti's family holding group CIR fell 3.46 percent to 692.7 lire after a fall in Cerus in Paris in which CIR holds a 49 percent stake. Cerus fell after industrial group CGIP denied plans it would launch a takeover of Cerus.

Dealers said early trading had been effected by the temporary suspension of derivatives trading this morning due to technical problems, but the overall market trend was downwards in a general lack of buying interest.
"There's very little interest out there and the Olivetti bounce was expected after the heavy falls," one trader said.
Among the blue-chips, Fiat slipped 1.79 percent to 4,381 lire after a falling 2.04 percent on Tuesday following a decline in Italian August car registrations of 7.50 percent.
Other shares were marked lower with ENI off 0.35 percent at 6,572 lire and Montedison down 0.8 percent at 929.1 lire.
Parmalat continued weak, 2.63 percent off at 1,885 lire, on continued health worries linked to mascarpone cheese, although Parmalat said none of its products were linked to these health concerns.
